# `silk/markdown/document`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A source-spanned Markdown tree with indexed nodes and borrowed source text.

## When to use

Parse strict CommonMark with `MarkdownDocument.parse`, or select extensions with `MarkdownOptions` and `MarkdownDocument.parseWithOptions`.
Walk the tree or render it with `silk.markdown.html`.

## Details

The document borrows its UTF-8 source. Verbatim text uses source ranges; decoded text uses one owned buffer.
Node ids belong to one document. Every span counts bytes in the original source, including syntax delimiters.

## Examples

### Inspect a heading and its source span

```silk
import silk.markdown.document { MarkdownDocument, MarkdownNodeId }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let document = run MarkdownDocument.parse("# Hello")
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let heading = MarkdownNodeId { index: 1 }
  if MarkdownDocument.headingLevel(&document, heading) != 1
    || MarkdownDocument.span(&document, heading).end != 7 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `MarkdownDocument` with `import silk.markdown.document { MarkdownDocument }`.

<a id="MarkdownDocument"></a>

## `MarkdownDocument`

```silk
pub struct MarkdownDocument<'source>
```

A parsed Markdown tree that borrows the source and owns decoded text and a flat node arena.

### Details

Verbatim literals are views into the original source. Decoded literals borrow one owned side buffer.
Returned text cannot outlive the document. Invalid ids return absent links, empty text, and zero payloads.
Footnote definitions follow main blocks in first-reference order. Unused definitions follow referenced definitions.

<a id="MarkdownDocument.impl"></a>

## Implementation `MarkdownDocument<'source>`

<a id="MarkdownDocument.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(source: string<'source>) -> MarkdownDocument<'source>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses strict CommonMark 0.31.2 with a nesting bound of 256 and every extension disabled. Every input produces a document.
The document borrows `source` and owns its nodes and decoded text.

#### Details

Bounded inline lookahead and reference expansion leave excess candidates as literal text.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the allocator cannot supply the tree or decoded text.

<a id="MarkdownDocument.impl.parseWithOptions"></a>

### Associated function `parseWithOptions`

```silk
pub effect fn parseWithOptions(
    source: string<'source>,
    options: &MarkdownOptions,
  ) -> MarkdownDocument<'source>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses UTF-8 Markdown with the extension switches and nesting bound in `options`.
Disabled extensions retain CommonMark syntax. Excess nesting remains literal text or paragraph content.
The document borrows `source` and owns its nodes and decoded text.

#### Details

Bounded inline lookahead and reference expansion leave excess candidates as literal text.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the allocator cannot supply the tree or decoded text.

<a id="MarkdownDocument.impl.literal"></a>

### Method `literal`

```silk
pub fn literal<'a>(self: &'a Self, id: MarkdownNodeId) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the literal of Text, Code, CodeBlock, HtmlBlock, or HtmlInline; returns empty text for other kinds.
The result borrows the document. Text has decoded backslash escapes and character references.
Code spans replace line endings with spaces and remove one enclosing space when required.
Block literals normalize line endings to line feeds. All literals replace NUL with U+FFFD.
